archetype: Cooldown-driven bossing thief that steals and re-uses Explorer skills. Its damage comes from cycling short-cooldown skills (above all Tempest) as often as possible, so cooldown reduction and cooldown-skip are treated as damage stats rather than utility. The class doc presents it as a class that clears bosses at low investment and is therefore favoured as a Legion champion / boss mule, at the cost of needing a hyper-skill swap roughly every minute to hold peak damage.

gearingNotes:
Phantom's gearing is unusual in three ways, all of them well sourced.

1. CRITICAL RATE IS SELF-SUPPLIED AND CAPS EARLY. The class doc publishes a full accounting of how a GMS Phantom reaches exactly 100% crit: 5% base, 35% from the Piercing Vision passive, 20% from its own Phantom Link at Lv.3, 10% from Lynn Link Lv.3, 10% from Decent Sharp Eyes, 4% from the Night Lord Lv.200 legion member bonus, 4% from the Marksman Lv.200 legion member bonus, 1% from an Ocean (Esfera) or Holy (Cernium) badge, and 11% from Hyper Stats at level 8. The wiki independently confirms the two largest in-class contributors - Piercing Vision at max gives Critical Rate +35% and Final Damage +30%, and Phantom Instinct at Lv.3 gives Critical Rate +20% plus Damage +5%. The practical consequence is the doc's own advice: push crit onto the Legion Grid and Legion Artifact so you can DROP hyper stat crit levels and spend those points elsewhere. Any generic 'max crit rate hyper stat' advice is actively wrong for this class.

2. COOLDOWN REDUCTION IS A DAMAGE STAT, AND A CD HAT IS THE RECOMMENDED HAT. The class doc recommends a cooldown-reduction hat paired with the Lv.200 Mercedes legion member bonus, and publishes a conversion table of cooldown to equivalent final damage (estimated, by the doc's own note, via Maple Scouter): -5s CD is about 6.0% FD; -4s CD plus one line of LUK% is also about 6.0% FD; -4s CD alone about 5.1% FD; -3s CD plus one line LUK% about 4.8% FD; -2s CD plus two lines LUK% about 4.2% FD; -3s CD alone about 3.9% FD; -2s CD plus one line LUK% about 3.4% FD; three lines of LUK% about 2.8% FD; -2s CD alone about 2.5% FD. The doc also tabulates the resulting cooldowns with a Lv.250 Mercedes: Tempest with the Cooldown Cutter hyper passive falls from 13.536s at base to 9.268s at -5s CD; Ace in the Hole from 14.1s to 9.55s; Rift Break, Phantom's Mark and Rose Finale from 28.2s to 23.2s. Without the Mercedes bonus, Tempest's base cooldown is 18s (14.4s with the hyper).

3. IGNORE DEFENSE IS UNUSUALLY HIGH FROM THE KIT. The class doc puts Phantom's innate combined IED at about 44.8%, from Priere D'Aria's passive 30% (+1% with Decent Combat Orders) plus Tempest's 20% one-minute debuff; Grandis' own skill-derived table independently lists Ignore DEF +44%, and the wiki confirms the two components (Priere D'Aria Lv.30: Damage +45%, Ignore Defense 30%; Tempest Lv.30: Enemy DEF Ignored 20% for 60s). A Phantom therefore needs less IED from gear and potential than a class starting from zero.

OTHER GEARING FACTS. Attack speed from the class's own passives is 7 (+5 base, +2 Cane Booster - the doc's own table, corroborated by Grandis), and the doc's stacking table adds Decent Speed Infusion +1, Extreme Green Potion +1 (exceeds the soft cap of +9) and Inner Ability or Real Speed Infusion +1 (reaches the hard cap of +10). The doc considers attack speed largely wasted on Phantom for bossing. Phantom has no Final Attack skill, which the class doc calls out explicitly - 'Phantom does not have any Final Attack and thus, gain no value boosting Final Attack Skill Damage %' - because it means that Legion Artifact line is worth nothing to this class. Tempest's attacks are always critical hits (wiki), which is part of why crit rate saturates so easily. The class's legion effect is %Mesos Obtained rather than a damage stat. Recommended familiar badges per the class doc: Ocean (+1% Damage, +1% Crit Rate, easily obtained), Apocalypse, Lion, Holy, Labyrinth and Showa.

STOLEN SKILLS ARE A REAL PROGRESSION AXIS. Phantom equips stolen Explorer skills into Impeccable Memory slots I through IV plus a Hyper tier, managed with Skill Swipe and Loadout. The wiki records the hard mechanical constraints: passive effects of stolen skills do not work, a skill may only go into a slot of equal or higher rank, a skill cannot be used immediately after being assigned, Bishop's Heal has its cooldown increased when stolen, and the stolen skill's level is capped by the Impeccable Memory slot's level. The class doc's boost-node captions add that Impeccable Memory boost nodes raise stolen-skill DAMAGE only and do nothing for stolen buff effects. Final Cut (a stolen skill) is the buff the doc's buff-duration advice is built around, and the doc names Arrow Blaster as the occupant of the Impeccable Memory III slot in its tri-node notes. A planner that models Phantom without a stolen-skill loadout slot is missing a system unique to the class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading the class doc's Legion Artifact priority list as if it were the HEXA Stat priority.
commonMistakes.detail: The doc lists Legion Artifact stats, under the heading 'Legion Artifact Stats in order of greatest to lowest priority', as Damage, Boss Damage, Crit Damage, All Stat, ATT/MATT, Cooldown Skip, Item Drop Rate, EXP, IED, Critical Chance, Buff Duration, Meso. Its HEXA Stat guidance is a different and shorter list: ATT, then Critical Damage, then LUK. These are two different systems in two different sections and have been conflated in at least one secondary summary of this doc.

commonMistakes.mistake: Maxing the Critical Rate hyper stat.
commonMistakes.detail: Phantom reaches 100% crit with the Critical Rate hyper stat at only level 8. The class doc's advice runs the other way - reduce that hyper stat level by taking crit from the Legion Grid and Legion Artifact instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a boost node trio list published before v.269 without checking it against the current groupings.
commonMistakes.detail: Grandis Library's Phantom page carries a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which is direct evidence Phantom's boost node groupings changed at that patch. mastermysty's widely-linked cross-class trio table is dated 2024-11-21 and therefore describes the old groupings. NUANCED 2026-09-12: the two do NOT disagree everywhere. Grandis' current 'Primary Trio' (Mille Aiguilles / Carte Blanche-Carte Noir / Tempest) is identical to mastermysty's 2024 bossing trio, so that one survived the regrouping. The mobbing trio did change - Grandis' current 'Secondary Trio' is Impeccable Memory III / Impeccable Memory IV / Rose Carte Finale, where mastermysty had Impeccable Memory II in place of IV.

commonMistakes.mistake: Demoting the Rose Carte Finale or Mille Aiguilles boost node groups.
commonMistakes.detail: ADDED 2026-09-12 after a mis-tiering was found in this file's own previous revision. Grandis tiers FOUR node groups as PRIMARY, not one: Node 1 Tempest, Node 2 Mille Aiguilles + Blason + Double Entendre, Node 3 Carte Blanche, Node 4 Rose Carte Finale + Penombre. All four unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery, which is what PRIMARY means on that page. Only Node 5 (Rapier Wit / Calling Card / Mille Cartes) is OTHER; Node 6 (Impeccable Memory I-IV) is SECONDARY. Treating Rose Carte Finale as a low-priority node is directly contradicted by the class doc's own efficiency table, where Rose Carte Finale VI level 1 is the single best HEXA purchase available to this class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Placing the ATT HEXA Stat on the highest-level slot by reflex.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc specifically warns that the slot giving the most ATT is not necessarily the highest-level slot, and says to place ATT by actual ATT yield first, then Critical Damage on the next-highest level, then LUK.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying the Interactive HEXA order on a Heroic character.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc's upgrade table is split into a fragment-limited Heroic column and an energy-limited Interactive column, and they diverge from the fifth purchase. Defying Fate levels 2-4 sit seventh on Interactive; on Heroic, Defying Fate level 2 alone is twenty-second.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling attack speed on Inner Ability.
commonMistakes.detail: Phantom is already at attack speed 7 from its own passives, and the class doc states outright that it is not recommended for Phantoms to go out of their way to obtain a +1 Attack Speed Inner Ability, even for training, because its hurricane bossing attacks gain only cast-animation speed from it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Chasing buff duration past Final Cut's 100% uptime expecting more damage.
commonMistakes.detail: The class doc's own threshold note is that beyond full Final Cut uptime, extra buff duration buys you a held iframe, not extra damage.

consensusAssessment:
Three sources independent of one another were reached - the class doc, mastermysty's node table, and maplestorywiki. But they are not three independent JUDGEMENT sources, and the file is labelled accordingly: no endgame recommendation in this file carries 'strong' consensus, because none has three independent sources behind it.

MECHANICAL FACTS (skill names, crit and IED contributions, cooldowns, attack speed, link and legion effects) are solid: independently confirmed across the class doc, the wiki and Grandis' API-derived stat table. The wiki's V Skills and HEXA Skills sections were finally read on 2026-09-12 via the api.php endpoint, so every 5th- and 6th-job node name in this file is now wiki-validated and no name here is an extraction artifact.

JUDGEMENT (HEXA investment order, 5th-job node priority, inner ability, hyper skill passives, HEXA stat placement, boost node tiering) rests on ONE current source, the Phantom class doc. Grandis Library restates that same doc by its own admission and is not a second vote; every claim that cites both is labelled sourceCount 1.

The ONE exception is the bossing boost node trio (Mille Aiguilles / Carte Blanche-Carte Noir / Tempest), which Grandis lists as its current Primary Trio and which mastermysty independently listed in 2024. That claim is sourceCount 2, consensus moderate - the strongest endgame claim in the file.

The HEXA order - the most valuable content here - is single-source and labelled weak. It is unusually well-founded for a single source (an explicit efficiency model, a stated boss benchmark of Hard Limbo phase 1, a named compiler, its own date of 2025-09-29, and a Heroic/Interactive split), and a planner should surface it as one class-community model rather than as settled consensus.

No hyper stat priority exists for Phantom in any reachable source, and that field is correctly null.

conflicts.positionA: mastermysty (2024-11-21): Bossing = Mille Aiguilles / Carte Blanc / Tempest; Mobbing = Rose Carte Finale / Impeccable Memory II / Impeccable Memory III; Trio #3 = Penombre / Impeccable Memory I / Impeccable Memory IV.
conflicts.positionB: Grandis Library (v.269, restating the class doc): Primary Trio = Mille Aiguilles / Carte Blanche-Carte Noir / Tempest; Secondary Trio = Impeccable Memory III / Impeccable Memory IV / Rose Carte Finale.
conflicts.status: PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-09-12. The bossing trio is not in conflict at all - the two sources give the same three skills, across the v.269 regrouping, from independent lineages. The mobbing trio does differ by one member (Impeccable Memory II vs IV), which is consistent with the regrouping rather than with genuine disagreement, since Grandis exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle. This was still NOT verified against a v.269 patch note, so both mobbing positions are recorded and the current one is the one presented.

conflicts.topic: The third hyper skill passive pick
conflicts.positionA: Grandis Library lists three co-equal options: Impeccable Memory - Reinforce, Persist, or Enhance.
conflicts.positionB: The class doc describes all three under its 'Recommended' heading, but its final AND/OR selection chain reads only '... AND Impeccable Memory - Persist OR Impeccable Memory - Enhance', with Reinforce characterised separately as 'normal 15% damage, use if it makes a difference in mobbing rates'.
conflicts.status: NARROWED 2026-09-12. The previous revision of this file overstated this conflict by asserting that the class doc does not include Reinforce in its recommended block; it does, as one of three described options. The remaining, smaller difference is that the doc's final selection chain omits Reinforce and Grandis' flat list does not. Most likely Grandis flattened the doc's conditional guidance. Not a substantive disagreement about what to press.

conflicts.topic: The class doc's own effective date
conflicts.positionA: The doc header states 'LAST UPDATED : 06-19-2025' with 'Update WIP: 6/11/2026'.
conflicts.positionB: The doc's changelog table runs to 11-24-2025, and the HEXA upgrade order section carries its own heading date of 09-29-2025.
conflicts.status: Internally inconsistent. This file treats the doc as current to 2025-11-24 and the HEXA order as current to 2025-09-29, because dated changelog entries are better evidence than a header line. Either way the doc predates v.271 and has not been confirmed against it.

conflicts.topic: Whether the origin skill is built early
conflicts.positionA: The generic cross-class advice circulating on aggregator sites is to activate mastery nodes, then boost nodes, then HEXA stat, with the origin skill treated as an early cornerstone.
conflicts.positionB: The Phantom class doc's Heroic efficiency model places Defying Fate level 2 twenty-second in the purchase order, behind four mastery unlocks, many mastery levels and three of the four enhancement nodes.
conflicts.status: Recorded, not resolved. Only the class doc's position is sourced to a Phantom-specific model; the generic position was not verified from any source that analysed Phantom. A planner should show the class doc's order and should not blend it with generic advice.

gaps: No hyper stat priority order exists for Phantom in any reachable source. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12 by full-text grep of the class doc: 'hyper stat' appears exactly twice, neither time as an allocation section. Grandis publishes none for any class. Field left null deliberately.

Grandis Library's Phantom 6th-job infographics ('6th Job (Main/Legion Champ)', credited 'Phantom Discord, based on (5 origin cycle, ~30 min)', and '6th Job (Mule)', credited 'Phantom Discord, based on (1 origin cycle, <6 min)') are dated 2026-09-04 - NEWER than every other source in this file. Their file references are /phantom/phantom-6th-job-main.png and /phantom/phantom-6th-job-mule.png, but they are lazy-loaded and every path probed on that host returned 404, so they could not be downloaded or read. For other classes these carry per-play-pattern HEXA investment order, so they are the single most promising unread Phantom artifact and may supersede the 2025-09-29 order.

The class doc's 'Stolen Skill Library' section is effectively empty as text - it consists of images and carries its own note that Pathfinder is missing. No recommended stolen-skill loadout for training or bossing could be extracted, despite this being Phantom's most class-unique decision. The doc does name Arrow Blaster in the Impeccable Memory III slot, which is the only stolen-skill datapoint recovered. This needs a vision pass over the doc or a read of the Phantom Discord.

The class doc's 93-row HEXA efficiency table is dated 2025-09-29 and covers only nine nodes: Defying Fate, the four masteries, and the four enhancements. The wiki lists further Phantom HEXA skills that appear nowhere in that table - Sol Hecate (Styx / Charon / Phlegethon / Pactum), La Mort Carte and Moonlit Serenade. The class doc describes 'Lmao Carte VI' (La Mort Carte) and 'Fate Shuffle VI' in its skill descriptions but gives them no position in the purchase order. So the order is silent on them; do not infer one. There is still no Sol Janus or Ascent guidance anywhere for Phantom.
The V-matrix example matrices and the 'Ideal Hexa Matrix Setup Example' are images; exact target node levels were not extractable.

reddit.com is blocked in this environment, so r/Maplestory Phantom threads were not examined at all. The Phantom Discord is not machine-readable. Both are named good-source-types and are unexamined, which is the main reason no endgame claim here reaches three independent sources.
Nothing was verified against v.271 itself. Every judgement source here is v.269-era or older, with the sole exception of the two Grandis infographics dated 2026-09-04, which could not be read.
sourcePatchCoverage: Best judgement source is current to roughly v.269 (class doc changelog 2025-11-24; HEXA order 2025-09-29). Grandis is stamped v.269, though its unread infographics are stamped 2026-09-04. The independent node source is 2024-11-21. No source consulted was confirmed against v.271.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionMethod: Every defect touching vMatrix / hexa / hyperSkills / hyperStats / innerAbility was settled by re-opening the exact cited page and re-reading the exact disputed claim. No new sources were sought. In addition, every remaining endgame claim was re-read against its cited source and re-labelled with sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt.

resolved.defect: THE BOOST NODE TIERING IS MISATTRIBUTED TO GRANDIS. The critic reported Grandis' tiers as Node 1 PRIMARY, Node 2 PRIMARY, Node 3 SECONDARY, Node 4 SECONDARY, Node 5 OTHER, Node 6 OTHER, against the file's Node 2 and 3 = secondary and Nodes 4, 5, 6 = other.
resolved.finding: The critic was right that the file was wrong, but the critic's replacement tiering was also wrong. Prose readings of this page produced three different answers across three passes, so the tiering was taken from the page's embedded __NEXT_DATA__ JSON, which is unambiguous: 'primary':[0,1,2,3], 'secondary':[5], 'other':[4] - zero-based indices into the node list. Cross-checked against the tier chip colours in the rendered HTML: Nodes 1-4 carry #2E94B6, Node 5 carries #6C757D, Node 6 carries #CC6A2A - three distinct colours matching three tiers, with Nodes 1-4 sharing one. The correct tiering is PRIMARY = Nodes 1, 2, 3 and 4; SECONDARY = Node 6 (Impeccable Memory I-IV); OTHER = Node 5 (Rapier Wit / Calling Card / Mille Cartes). This is also internally coherent: Phantom has exactly four HEXA masteries, and Grandis defines PRIMARY as the nodes that unlock one.
resolved.whatChanged: boostNodeGroups rebuilt with the correct membership; Grandis' three tier definitions added verbatim. Also deleted a related false attribution: the file had said Grandis 'flags [Node 1] as the one tied to unlocking the HEXA mastery'. Grandis says no such thing about Node 1 specifically - the PRIMARY definition applies to all four primary nodes. A commonMistakes entry was added warning against demoting the Rose Carte Finale or Mille Aiguilles node groups, since that was the actionable harm.

resolved.defect: Link skill numbers are unverified and partly contradicted. The file states 'Lv.1 Critical Rate +10%. Lv.3 Critical Rate +20% and Damage +5%', sourced only to maplestorywiki.net which returns HTTP 403; Grandis states +5% Damage and +15-20% Crit Rate, i.e. no level in the range is +10%.
resolved.section: linkSkill - outside the five endgame sections, but resolved because it became cheap to settle once wiki access was restored
resolved.finding: The claim is correct and the critic's reading of Grandis was the error. maplestorywiki was reached through the MediaWiki API with a browser User-Agent, which returns HTTP 200 where the rendered page 403s. The Phantom Instinct SkillBox carries formula 'Critical Rate: +{#expr:5+5*x}%' with masterLevel=3, and formula2 'Critical Rate: +{#expr:5+5*x}%, Damage: +{#expr:5*log3(x)}%' at formula2Level=3. Evaluated: Lv.1 +10%, Lv.2 +15%, Lv.3 +20% crit, and 5*log3(3) = +5% damage at Lv.3. Grandis' link-skill block shows 'Lv. 2: +15%' and 'Lv. 3: +20%' plus '+5%' damage - it omits a Lv.1 row rather than contradicting one, and the two sources agree on every level they both state.
resolved.whatChanged: linkSkill.effect restated as the wiki's actual formula rather than two cherry-picked levels; sources, sourceCount 2, consensus moderate, verifiedAt and a verificationNote added. The wiki access route was recorded in the sources block so the 403 does not block future passes, and the gap entry claiming the wiki's V Skills / HEXA Skills sections were unreachable was removed because those sections have now been read.

additionalCorrectionsFoundDuringResoluti.finding:
The previous revision recorded only mastermysty's three 2024 trios and labelled all three 'stale-single-source'. Grandis in fact publishes a CURRENT (v.269) recommended-trio block that the previous pass missed entirely: 'Primary Trio' = Mille Aiguilles + Tempest + Carte Blanche/Carte Noir, 'Secondary Trio' = Impeccable Memory III + Impeccable Memory IV + Rose Carte Finale, with three notes. Grandis' Primary Trio is identical to mastermysty's Bossing trio, which makes that one trio the only endgame claim in this file with two genuinely independent sources. Also: mastermysty labels its third row 'Trio #3', not 'additional'. Also: mastermysty's Phantom cells carry real text names in

tags alongside the icons, so those trio names are NOT an image-extraction artifact, which was a live risk.

The Impeccable Memory III note had inverted the doc's polarity. The doc reads 'Arrow Blaster is optional, provides additional coverage if the user's main mobbing skill is 1-shot without 20% Final Damage'; the file had paraphrased it as 'when the main mobbing skill CANNOT one-shot'. The doc's sentence is ambiguous as written, so it is now quoted rather than resolved by this file.

Every one of the 22 recorded steps and all 25 efficiency values were re-read against the doc's Heroic column and match exactly; the column was confirmed strictly descending with no inversions, and the table confirmed at 93 rows per column (186 percentage cells). One claim was overstated: step 4 said the first three mastery unlocks are 'each worth about five times as much per fragment'. Actual ratios are 8.6x, 5.5x and 4.8x. Corrected to the real numbers. The per-step FD values are now stored in an fdPerFragment field so the claim is checkable.

Boss Damage / Ignore Defense / Damage were stored as a bare ordered array, but the doc gives them as three unranked bullets under 'The following stats will be used in the 4th~6th Hexa Stats when they get unlocked'. Array position would have invented a ranking. Now carries ordered:false and an explicit note. hexaStats.firstThree keeps ordered:true because the doc DOES state that sequence.

firstLine and secondThirdLines were bare ordered arrays where the doc gives unranked option lists; both now carry ordered:false with a note explaining why Chance to Skip Cooldown is nevertheless listed first (the doc calls it 'the Popular and viable option' and leads its Current BIS row with it). exampleSetups keeps ordered:true because the doc's 'Current BIS:' line sits directly above the first row. Separately, attackSpeedLine said the doc credits 'windup and cast animations'; the doc says cast animation only, and the file had omitted both the doc's strongest supporting sentence ('It is not recommended for Phantoms to go out of their way to obtain a +1 Attack Speed Inner Ability, even if just for training') and its two stated exceptions. All corrected.

The file asserted that the class doc 'does not include [Impeccable Memory - Reinforce] in its own recommended block' and built a conflict with Grandis on that basis. The doc DOES describe Reinforce under its 'Recommended' heading, as the third of three Impeccable Memory options; it is only absent from the doc's final AND/OR chain. The conflict is real but much narrower than recorded, and has been restated.

Stored as a bare array where the doc gives a flat unranked caption list; now carries ordered:false. Also, the doc writes '+5 matrix enhancement for +? All Stat' and '+? Attack' with a literal question mark - the magnitudes are unstated in the source and are now recorded as unstated rather than silently smoothed over.

With wiki access restored, Phantom's full HEXA skill list was read for the first time. Every node name used in hexa.order is wiki-validated. But the wiki also lists Sol Hecate (Styx / Charon / Phlegethon / Pactum), La Mort Carte and Moonlit Serenade as Phantom HEXA skills, none of which appear anywhere in the doc's 2025-09-29 efficiency table - a real and previously unrecorded gap in the investment order. Also recorded: the Grandis infographics are dated 2026-09-04, newer than any other source here, and could not be downloaded from any probed path.

contest.shipReadyBasis: Both logged defects are settled - one corrected, one confirmed - and every claim in vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats and innerAbility has been re-read against its cited source on 2026-09-12 and labelled with sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt. No claim in those five sections now points at a source that does not support it, no node or skill name in them is unverified against the wiki, and no array in them implies a ranking its source declines to state. What remains are labelled GAPS (absent guidance) rather than unverified claims. Ship-ready here means honestly labelled, not well corroborated: consensus across the five endgame sections is 'weak' everywhere except the bossing boost node trio, which is 'moderate'.
